Senses.PreferredTarget: put another head atop one's head
AlternateTargets: add a head on top of the head
set a head upon one's head
Senses.Explanation: Putting another head atop one's head is an image of needless addition to what is already complete. Chan records apply it when an interlocutor adds a name, assertion, attainment, or operation, and directly compare it with drawing feet on a snake, adding frost to snow, and fastening a shackle onto a cangue. Linji Yixuan follows it with the question, "what do you lack?" (是儞欠少甚麼). Baohua Xian pairs "you have finished eating gruel—putting another head atop your head" (喫粥了也，頭上安頭) with "go wash your bowl—drawing feet on a snake" (洗鉢盂去，為虵畫足). Yun'an Zhenjing separately calls his own added words "drawing feet on a snake" (為蛇畫足). Other explicit parallels are Jingyin Facheng's "add frost atop snow" (霜加雪上) and Ruiyan Zihong's "put a shackle on a cangue" (枷上著杻). These corpus comparisons establish unnecessary addition without importing an external theory.
Senses.Note: The phrase is productive in binary naming tests: calling an object a staff may be "putting another head atop one's head," while denying it is a staff may be "cutting off the head to seek life" (斬頭覓活). Saying "mind itself is Buddha" (即心是佛) is likewise compared to putting another head atop one's head, while saying "neither mind nor Buddha" (非心非佛) is compared to losing the head and recognizing its shadow (迷頭認影). One community address explicitly lists "do not put another head atop your head" (不得頭上安頭) as the fourth of four ailments, after seeking another's spittle along the road, driving a stake while rocking an oar, and cutting off the head to seek life. The term names none of those other expressions; their value here is the corpus's own contrast set.

Occurrences.Kwic: 瞎漢頭上安頭，是儞欠少甚麼？
Occurrences.AttributionNote: The Linked-Lamp Compendium (聯燈會要), section on Linji Yixuan: Linji Yixuan says blind fellows put another head atop their heads and asks what they lack.

Occurrences.Kwic: 第四不得頭上安頭。能離四病，自然天下太平。
Occurrences.AttributionNote: The Complete Collection of the Five Lamps, volumes 34–120 (五燈全書(第34卷-第120卷)), section on Baiyun Wuliang Cang: Baiyun Wuliang Cang makes the phrase the fourth of four ailments and says leaving the four brings peace under heaven. Baiyun Wuliang Cang is source-attested but not yet in the roster.

Occurrences.Kwic: 上堂：喫粥了也，頭上安頭。洗鉢盂去，為虵畫足。
Occurrences.AttributionNote: The Complete Collection of the Five Lamps, volumes 34–120 (五燈全書(第34卷-第120卷)), section on Baohua Xian: Baohua Xian pairs finishing gruel with putting another head atop the head and washing the bowl with drawing feet on a snake. Baohua Xian is source-attested but not yet in the roster.

Occurrences.Kwic: 若向這裏說即心是佛，大似頭上安頭；若說非心非佛，何異迷頭認影？
Occurrences.AttributionNote: The Linked-Lamp Compendium (聯燈會要), section on Shaolin En: Shaolin En compares saying mind itself is Buddha to putting another head atop one's head, and saying neither mind nor Buddha to losing the head and recognizing its shadow. Shaolin En is source-attested but not yet in the roster.

Occurrences.Kwic: 舉拳曰：還見麼？師曰：見。悟曰：頭上安頭。
Occurrences.AttributionNote: The Complete Collection of the Five Lamps, volumes 34–120 (五燈全書(第34卷-第120卷)), biography of Huqiu Shaolong: Yuanwu Keqin raises his fist, asks whether Huqiu sees it, and answers Huqiu's yes with the verdict 'putting another head atop one's head.'

Occurrences.Kwic: 豎拂子，曰：若喚作拂子，頭上安頭；不喚作拂子，斬頭覓活。
Occurrences.AttributionNote: The Complete Collection of the Five Lamps, volumes 34–120 (五燈全書(第34卷-第120卷)), section on Sanmei Faru Le: Sanmei Faru Le contrasts naming the whisk as putting another head atop one's head with refusing the name as cutting off the head to seek life. Sanmei Faru Le is source-attested but not yet in the roster.

Occurrences.Kwic: 更待長老開口動舌，又堪作什麼？老僧恁麼道，也是為蛇畫足。
Occurrences.AttributionNote: The Complete Collection of the Five Lamps, volumes 34–120 (五燈全書(第34卷-第120卷)), section on Yun'an Zhenjing Kewen: Zhenjing Kewen says that waiting for the elder to add speech is useless and that his own wording is drawing feet on a snake.

Occurrences.Kwic: 妙圓超悟，頭上安頭；頓獲法身，枷上著杻。
Occurrences.AttributionNote: The Linked-Lamp Compendium (聯燈會要), section on Ruiyan Zihong: Ruiyan Zihong pairs complete awakening with putting another head atop one's head and suddenly obtaining the teaching-body with putting a shackle on a cangue. Ruiyan Zihong is source-attested but not yet in the roster.

Occurrences.Kwic: 認作空劫時，自己分明頭上安頭，更言落在今時，何異霜加雪上？
Occurrences.AttributionNote: The Linked-Lamp Compendium (聯燈會要), section on Jingyin Facheng: Jingyin Facheng says taking it as the time of the empty eon is putting another head atop one's head, and adding that it falls in the present is adding frost atop snow. Jingyin Facheng is source-attested but not yet in the roster.

Occurrences.Kwic: 進云：「滿目盡是青山綠水。如何是道？」師云：「字水深。」進云：「自性了然。如何是佛？」師云：「頭上安頭。」進云：「三藏拈向一邊。如何是法？」師云：「斬頭覓活。」
Occurrences.AttributionNote: The Recorded Sayings of Chan Master Huayan Shengke (華嚴聖可禪師語錄): Huayan Shengke answers a question about buddha with 'put another head atop one's head' and a question about the teaching with 'cut off the head to seek life.' Huayan Shengke is source-attested but not yet in the roster.

Occurrences.Kwic: 見山不是山、見水不是水，雖然透得一切法空，未免頭上安頭，法身死水。
Occurrences.AttributionNote: The Recorded Sayings of Chan Master Chaozong (朝宗禪師語錄): Chaozong Tongren says that seeing mountains as not mountains and waters as not waters, even after passing through the emptiness of all things, remains putting another head atop one's head. Chaozong Tongren is source-attested but not yet in the roster.
